ARIADNA RETRIEVAL BASELINE COMPARISON REPORT V1.0

1. Objective

This report compares BM25, dense retrieval, and hybrid retrieval on the corrected ARIADNA split. Earlier results obtained from a split affected by leakage are retained only for auditing and are not used to compare systems.

The main evaluation uses recall@10, MRR, latency, and analysis by category. Experiments use 256-token chunks, three seeds where applicable, and the corpus freeze date recorded in the manifest.

2. Systems

BM25 serves as the lexical baseline and uses title, tags, and text. Dense retrieval uses a multilingual model. The hybrid system combines lexical and dense scores and applies lightweight reranking. Configurations share the same document collection and version filters.

3. Overall results

BM25 achieves recall@10 of 0.69, MRR of 0.52, and median latency of 74 ms. Hybrid retrieval achieves recall@10 of 0.80, MRR of 0.63, and median latency of 182 ms. Improvement is concentrated in semantic, multi-hop, and temporal questions. BM25 retains an advantage for exact identifiers and highly specific strings.

Detailed result 1

Analysis 1: direct questions. Results show that both systems retrieve sources containing explicit terms well. Recall, rank of the first relevant result, number of required sources, and latency are compared. Errors are manually reviewed to distinguish query, index, chunking, version, or relevance defects. Comparison uses confidence intervals and retains individual runs rather than the mean alone. A small difference is not presented as a definitive conclusion.
